rationale: Receipt 19867c5d7a784ca8afcec5890786dba3 confirms the StopSign flip: node 5 reports is_reconfigured true at decided 5, false at decided 4 after the reconnect sync (the declared comparison is violated), and still false at decided 5 after re-decision. That last observation implies the accepted index no longer equals 5; sync_log adds one for the StopSign on top of sync_idx plus suffix, so the StopSign is likely double-counted. This update asserts the flip, records the non-recovery, opens a gap on the accepted index, and requests a successor that samples accepted.

knowledge.statement: On the executed five-node run, node 5 reported is_reconfigured Some with decided 5 before the reconnect sync, is_reconfigured None with decided 4 immediately after the AcceptSync, and is_reconfigured None again after its decided index returned to 5 (decided_leader2 also 5).
knowledge.conditions: Five OmniPaxos instances, entries 1..4 decided everywhere, a reconfigure whose StopSign is accepted by 1,2,3,5 and decided only on node 5; node 1 cut, node 2 elected with promises from 3 and 4 at decided 4, node 5's Prepare lost and reconnected(2) driving PrepareReq/Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync.

gaps.question: What is node 5's accepted index after the StopSign sync, and does is_reconfigured ever return to Some once decided is back at 5?

interpretations.rationale: The authority-transition signal is unstable and does not recover in this run. Receipt 19867c5d7a784ca8afcec5890786dba3 ran decided_stopsign_flips_through_reconnect_sync (exit 0, test passed). Event 0 (ready) records node 5 at decided 5 with is_reconfigured true and node 2 at decided 4 with accepted 5, so the StopSign was decided on node 5 while the future leader's quorum had not decided it. Event 1 (after_sync) records decided 4 and is_reconfigured false; the single declared comparison (reconfig eq true at phase after_sync) is complete and violated, which is the flip. Event 2 (after_redecide) records decided 5 with decided_leader2 5 but is_reconfigured still false. With the StopSign still stored, is_reconfigured being false at decided 5 means the accepted index is no longer 5, and the source shows why: sync_log sets accepted to sync.sync_idx + suffix length and then adds one more when log_sync carries a StopSign, even though node 5's accepted prefix already included that StopSign (sync_idx was 5). The sync therefore lowers decided below the accepted StopSign and also advances accepted past the log's last index, so decided can never catch up and the reconfiguration never reads as decided again on that node. A user polling is_reconfigured sees a decided reconfiguration revert to not-decided indefinitely on this follower after a reconnect, while the rest of the cluster re-decides. The exact accepted value and whether any later sync repairs it are not yet measured, so they are recorded as a gap and the successor adds accepted to the sample.
counterevidence: If the reconnecting node's Promise participates in the prepare quorum, the leader's decided index covers the StopSign and the flip does not occur.
If the new leader's quorum already decided the StopSign, the accepted ledger and decided index agree and no flip occurs.
The StopSign value is preserved and the rest of the cluster re-decides index 5, so this is a status/authority-signal defect, not loss of the reconfiguration or divergence of values.
Whether the accepted index mismatch is permanent or repaired by a later sync is unmeasured; the third event suggests it persists through the re-decision.
limitations: The receipt does not sample accepted, so the double-count is inferred from is_reconfigured false at decided 5 plus the sync_log source; the successor measures it directly.
Five nodes, majority quorum, memory storage, unit batch and no snapshots; starting the new cluster and later resyncs are not exercised.
The user's reaction to the flip is not modeled; only is_reconfigured is measured.

scope.description: Same five-node StopSign scenario, with node 5's accepted index sampled at ready, after_sync and after_redecide in addition to decided and is_reconfigured.
assumptions: The StopSign for node 4 and the Decide messages to 2, 3 and 4 are lost, so only node 5 learns the decision before the reconnect.
The Accepted replies from 3 and 4 are held so node 2 cannot re-decide before node 5 reconnects.
No ticks are called; leadership is obtained with try_become_leader.
excluded: Snapshots, flexible quorums, batching, starting the new cluster and repeated reconnects.

experiment.prefix: Identical to the previous run: decide Value(1..=4) on all five nodes, reconfigure to configuration_id 2, deliver the AcceptStopSign to 2,3,5 and purge it for 4, deliver the Accepteds to node 1, deliver the Decide only to node 5, emit ready with decided, accepted and reconfig. Cut node 1, elect node 2, extract and discard the Prepare for node 5, settle promises from 3 and 4, deliver AcceptSyncs to 3 and 4 and hold their Accepted replies. Call node5.reconnected(2) and deliver the PrepareReq, Prepare, Promise and AcceptSync in order; emit after_sync with decided, accepted, reconfig, decided_leader2 and lost_prepare_count. Deliver the held Accepted replies, settle among nodes 2..5, emit after_redecide with decided, accepted and reconfig.

comparisons.description: After re-decision the StopSign occupies index 5, so accepted should be 5 and is_reconfigured should be true; the predicate is expected to be violated if sync_log double-counts the StopSign.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds node 5's accepted index to every event and a comparison requiring accepted to equal 5 (the StopSign index) after re-decision, so the suspected StopSign double count in sync_log is measured rather than inferred. Scenario and delivery control are unchanged.
